notes: Nikita Ltd. (1991-93) sliding/matching puzzle. No GAME.BAT; PUZZLE.EXE is the intended entry, with a companion CONFIG.COM in the folder. On boot PUZZLE.EXE shows 'SELECT PUZZLE DIMENSION' (a 3 x 3 / 4 x 4 list box, Toka-DOS default black background). Keyboard input DOES reach the game: {down}/{up} visibly move the highlight between the two items (confirmed via distinct frame hashes), and it holds the moved-to selection indefinitely with no further input -- this is genuine engine interactivity, not a frozen screen. However, {enter} on this screen never starts a puzzle: every attempt (isolated, after {down}, after {space}, with or without CONFIG.COM run first) produces one blank transient frame then lands on a screen that is either bit-identical to the very first dimension-select frame, or advances to a second screen, 'SELECT SOUND OUTPUT DEVICE' (a full-block list with Sound Blaster pre-highlighted, matching this machine's sound_blaster=true auto-detect) -- reached from dimension-select via {enter}. From sound-select, {enter} cycles back to dimension-select and {esc} exits the CURRENT program straight to a 'C:\GAME>' DOS prompt (confirmed with -NoLoop: a blinking-cursor prompt, no further screen). This dimension<->sound carousel is identical whether the running program is CONFIG.COM or PUZZLE.EXE itself, and choosing a non-default dimension or sound device does not change the outcome. CONFIG.COM was run as an experiment (chained 'CONFIG.COM\r\nPUZZLE.EXE', per the brief's 'run config.com only if the game demands configuration') to see whether it unblocks PUZZLE.EXE: it does not -- PUZZLE.EXE re-shows the identical dimension/sound wizard from scratch afterward and still cannot be advanced past it with any tried key ({enter}, {esc}, {space}, digits 1-4, y/n, {tab}, {f1}-{f2}, {shift}/{ctrl}/{alt}) or mouse (TOKAMOUS loaded, home/move/click onto the visible box: no effect, this menu appears keyboard-only). The likely cause: the shipped NIKITA.CFG in this corpus copy is an unfilled installer placeholder ('.\xxxxxxxx.xxx', 14 bytes), and PUZZLE.EXE's own string table contains 'Error: File NIKITA.CFG not found. Try to install this programm again.' -- this looks like a never-installed dump that expects a real installer to stamp NIKITA.CFG with an absolute path before the dimension/sound wizard can hand off to the actual puzzle board; CONFIG.COM (247 bytes, strings only reference CONFIG.DAT and puzzle.exe, never NIKITA.CFG) does not perform that step. Per AGENT-BRIEF.md this is recorded as a near-idle result: the recipe's schedule below is the shortest one that demonstrates real interactivity (down/up move the highlight; enter/esc drive the dimension<->sound carousel and one exit-to-DOS-and-reboot-via-AUTOEXEC cycle) inside the 120s deep-profile window, without ever reaching a playable puzzle grid. 486 chosen as the correct persona (real-mode-era DOS text-mode title, no protected-mode/3D need). Profile window covers: boot (0-2s) -> dimension-select idle with a highlight move and revert (2-16s) -> a failed dimension confirm that flickers back to the same menu (16-22s) -> a second dimension move (22-27s) -> a confirm that reaches SELECT SOUND OUTPUT DEVICE (27-33s) -> esc exits to a DOS prompt, AUTOEXEC loop restarts PUZZLE.EXE, landing back on dimension-select for the remainder of the 120s window (33-120s, one more down/enter/esc cycle repeats near 33-45s then idles). rt was 71.16 on the deep run, well above the 486 target of 5.0, so no -BarrierCensus was needed. Minor anomaly: emulator.log shows 6 open-bus reads and 6 writes across ports 0x216/0x21a/0x21e (unclaimed) -- consistent with a game-port/joystick hardware probe during startup, benign, not connected to the dimension/sound wizard issue.
